items.question: Which older documented Erosion and TileGate behaviors remain exact in GAEA 2.3.0.1?
resolvedParts: Current official Erosion2 documentation explicitly describes deterministic results.
Current official tiled-build documentation confirms that some operations require nonlocal context and some current node pages explicitly require baking for Hybrid/Tiled builds.
Current official non-determinism documentation shows that deterministic operation does not imply cross-resolution identity.
items.remainingUnknown: A current official TileGate reference or exact current legacy TileGate semantics was not found in the bounded R02 search.
items.currentBestView: Use the current-doc-backed abstraction of an operator context/locality signature. Do not depend on the legacy TileGate node name or claim its exact behavior survives in 2.3.
items.promotionBlock: Blocks only claims about exact legacy TileGate implementation; does not block the general operator-context transfer.

items.question: Can seam blending ever be used in KAOPU runtime presentation without being mistaken for truth continuity?
items.reason: GAEA uses blending as an engineering workaround for tiled processing, while KAOPU requires explicit shared-edge truth contracts.
items.currentBestView: Presentation-only blending may be allowed later, but never as evidence that shared truth is continuous.

items.question: Does a deterministic operator imply identical output across different resolutions?
items.answer: No. Current GAEA documentation separately documents deterministic Erosion2 behavior and resolution-dependent procedural differences. KAOPU determinism must therefore be scoped to an evaluation contract, while cross-resolution equivalence is a separate property requiring separate evidence.

items.question: How much agreement between multiple external AIs is informative when their training/source overlap is unknown?
items.currentBestView: Treat agreement as a search signal only, not independent evidence.

items.question: How much measurable cross-resolution error reduction will footprint-aware field evaluation produce in current KAOPU and Mother implementations?
items.known: Primary sources strongly support filtering/sampling-footprint control as an anti-aliasing requirement, and a KAOPU-compatible plane-wave footprint probe has been authored.
items.remainingUnknown: The new probe has not yet produced a promoted runtime result and no Mother-domain fixture has compared current versus footprint-aware evaluation.
items.currentBestView: Keep evaluationFootprint/filterPolicy as Candidate contract fields; require an executed probe and Mother fixture before candidate-complete or Frozen promotion.

items.question: Can unified output normalization improve interchangeability without corrupting amplitude or energy semantics?
items.reason: Mature tools expose normalization for convenience, but normalization changes value range and can erase physically meaningful amplitude relationships if applied silently.
items.currentBestView: Normalization must be explicit, typed, versioned, and downstream-aware. Never normalize a physical or evidence-bearing quantity merely to make operator outputs look interchangeable.

items.question: Should stochastic procedural-noise evaluation be adopted as a general KAOPU acceleration method?
items.reason: NVIDIA 2023 research demonstrates value in Monte Carlo rendering, but that estimator context does not automatically transfer to deterministic world state, simulation, collision, hydrology, or evidence reconstruction.
items.currentBestView: Keep renderer-specific only until a relevant Mother proves unbiasedness, temporal stability, deterministic replay requirements, and task error under its own contract.

items.question: What is the minimum physically meaningful atmosphere state that KAOPU should preserve without overfitting UE or Karma parameter interfaces?
items.known: R01-R02 primary-source review supports explicit planet/reference frame, neutral thermodynamic/species state, separate aerosol/cloud media, emitter/surface coupling, spectral-property semantics, path query, evaluator policy, and camera/display separation. R03 executable evidence shows that one state can support multiple evaluators whose authority differs by query geometry; evaluator validity must therefore be explicit rather than global. R04 adds a multi-root Earth fixture architecture and shows that ReferenceSampleKey must preserve source-required context dimensions through reduction. R05 clarifies evidence class and adds provenance-dependency/coverage semantics. R06 establishes that global modelDomain and per-output QuantityValidityEnvelope must remain distinct, and that unsupported values must be represented as typed Missing/Unsupported rather than ordinary numerics.
items.remainingUnknown: The exact canonical Earth schema, state-source hierarchy above 86 km, required unit types, authoritative cross-root numerical fixtures, and the complete dependency/coverage/quantity-validity graph for all candidate atmosphere products remain unresolved.
items.currentBestView: Keep the layered Reference-State -> State-Reducer -> Runtime-Packet -> Evaluator architecture Candidate. Preserve independent Observation Root IDs, EvidenceClass, EvidenceDependencyDAG, per-variable coverage/support metadata, modelDomain, QuantityValidityEnvelope, typed Missing/Unsupported, and a first-class ReferenceSampleKey. Require authoritative NRL numerical confirmation and authenticated spectral checkpoints before candidate-complete promotion.

items.question: Does KAOPU need a spectral reference layer for atmosphere, or is typed RGB coefficient storage sufficient for its intended world reconstruction and rendering tasks?
items.known: HITRAN provides wavelength-resolved molecular spectroscopy used for atmospheric transmission/emission, while modern atmosphere literature validates cheaper realtime approximations against higher-fidelity spectral references. NASA solar-irradiance material also shows strongly wavelength-dependent source and absorber behavior. This is sufficient to reject vendor RGB coefficients as the canonical definition of atmosphere spectrum. R04 further defines the minimum checkpoint metadata: spectral-coordinate convention, molecule/isotopologue, spectroscopy provenance, T/P, line-shape model, column/path state, units, and tolerance.
items.remainingUnknown: The wavelength domains, sampling/basis resolution, authenticated reference line subset, and task-specific RGB/few-band compression error budgets are not yet fixed.
items.currentBestView: Preserve spectral-reference capability and allow validated task-specific compression to RGB/few-band runtime packets. Do not require full spectral realtime evaluation by every Mother.

items.question: Should atmospheric refraction be included in the first KAOPU atmosphere core merely because it is an optical phenomenon?
items.answer: No. The reviewed current UE/Karma atmosphere cores are organized around participating-media scattering, absorption, extinction, transmittance, phase behavior, multiple scattering, and surface coupling. Refraction remains a real but separate process and should be added only when a concrete observable/process requires refractive-index gradients.

items.question: Where should KAOPU place the semantic boundary between neutral-atmosphere state and ionosphere/plasma/space-weather state for ground-to-space queries?
items.known: Current NRLMSIS is a neutral whole-atmosphere empirical model, while current NASA CCMC physics models such as GITM/TIE-GCM introduce ion/electron species, electrodynamics, winds and solar/geomagnetic forcing. NASA also notes there is no sharp atmosphere-to-space density boundary.
items.remainingUnknown: The smallest query contract that can couple neutral state to ionosphere/plasma effects without turning the first atmosphere core into a full space-weather simulator has not been defined or tested.
items.currentBestView: Keep ionosphere/plasma as a separate optional coupled state domain. Do not fake aurora, plasma or charged-particle physics by extending a neutral Rayleigh/Mie renderer.

items.question: Do the selected NRLMSIS 2.1 packaged test vectors reproduce exactly when executed from an authoritative NRL package or NASA CCMC host?
items.known: R04 inspected a non-authoritative mirror of the public NRL package and preserved its expected vectors only as Candidate. R05 re-confirmed the official NRL release location and current NASA CCMC 2.1 host. R06 confirmed that the official NRL tar/zip and Wiley S2/S3 supporting archives are discoverable and have matching nominal published sizes, but size equality is not artifact identity and no authoritative execution was obtained.
items.remainingUnknown: The official NRL/Wiley binary release still could not be materialized into the bounded R06 execution environment and the browser-hosted CCMC service was not converted into an unattended authoritative run, so no authoritative execution comparison was completed.
items.currentBestView: Keep mirrored numerical vectors Candidate. Matching filename/size is only a transport clue. Promotion requires authoritative package identity/execution or an authoritative hosted result for the locked query.

items.question: Which tiny authenticated HITRAN transition subset should become the first KAOPU optical regression fixture?
items.known: Official HITRAN documentation fixes spectral-coordinate and line-intensity semantics and shows that line shape depends on thermodynamic regime. R04 defines the checkpoint schema without inventing line values. R05-R06 retain the requirement for authenticated line retrieval before numerical promotion.
items.remainingUnknown: No authenticated transition tuple was retrieved in R06.
items.currentBestView: Do not synthesize or copy unverified line constants. Retrieve two or three authenticated lines later and bind molecule/isotopologue, line provenance, temperature, pressure, line-shape model, column/path state, units, tolerance, EvidenceClass and dependency provenance.

items.question: How should KAOPU represent evidence independence when measurements, holdouts, empirical models and retrieval products share instruments, fitted data, retrieval models or upstream priors?
items.known: R05 primary sources established that root identity and evidence independence are multidimensional. R06 adds a concrete sample-split result from the primary NRLMSIS 2.1 paper: 30 ensembles were divided into first-15 fitting and second-15 validation roles, but random sampling did not exclude duplicates, so observations may repeat within or across ensembles. Therefore validation labels do not guarantee observation-level disjointness. The paper also states final parameters were averaged from fitting ensembles 6-15 after five spin-up ensembles.
items.remainingUnknown: Complete transitive dependency graphs, shared calibration/prior dependencies and quantitative correlation among all candidate atmosphere products are not yet mapped. The official NRL sample README also overlaps NO.15 between tuning and validation ranges, while the 2022 paper describes first 15 versus second 15 ensembles; exact file-15 membership remains unresolved.
items.currentBestView: Use EvidenceDependencyDAG plus multidimensional independence metadata. Keep sample-split, instrument/source, retrieval-model and shared-prior dependence distinct; add samplingScheme, samplingWithReplacement, sampleOverlapStatus and parameterAggregationLineage. Unknown edges stay Unknown. Root identity and split labels must never be aliased to independence.
items.promotionBlock: Blocks claims of independent corroboration where dependencies/overlap are unresolved; does not by itself block using a model as a clearly labeled empirical reference state.

items.question: How should source-specific missing or unsupported atmosphere quantities propagate through KAOPU reducers and evaluators?
items.known: The primary NRLMSIS 2.1 paper states that NO output is missing below 72.5 km because of a fitted baseline-profile edge artifact even though the parent model accepts lower-altitude queries. A non-authoritative mirror exposes an exact numeric missing-density sentinel of 9.999e-38; that exact value remains Candidate. The R06 semantic probe shows that the sentinel has a finite logarithm, so an unmasked sentinel can survive numerical transforms and masquerade as physical structure.
items.remainingUnknown: Authoritative confirmation of the exact source sentinel and a generalized missing-value mapping across all selected atmosphere property providers are still unresolved.
items.currentBestView: Convert source-specific sentinels/unsupported outputs to typed Missing/Unsupported at ingestion, before units, logarithms, interpolation, normalization, reduction or optical calculations. Artifact-driven cutoffs are validity boundaries, not physical layers; source substitution across them must be explicit and provenance-bearing.
items.promotionBlock: Blocks any fixture that numerically transforms an unmasked missing sentinel; does not block other independently valid atmosphere observations.

items.question: Does the proposed MaterialGeneratorManifest replay identically in a locked Adobe Substance Engine across the intended resolution and seed matrix?
items.known: R32 official documentation fixes the required context categories and one-way SBSAR boundary. The source-semantic linter passed nine negative-control tests.
items.remainingUnknown: No sbscooker, sbsrender or Substance Designer executable was available; no SBS/SBSAR was cooked or rendered, no output hash was produced, and engine-version compatibility was not exercised.
items.currentBestView: Keep editable source identity, published evaluator identity, effective inherited context, output semantics and derived cache identity separate. Do not promote until one authoritative runtime fixture is executed.

items.question: Does the pinned COLMAP -> Brush -> uncompressed PLY -> constrained SPZ v4 -> Three.js r186 chain preserve a real KAOPU static-object reconstruction within accepted geometric, appearance and device budgets?
items.known: R33-R40 authenticated the principal handoff, range/envelope/DC/SH/antialias/sorting and constructor-memory contracts. R41 executed Niantic v4 encoding, Three r186 public parsing and its actual ZSTD decoder. Loader decoded streams require 20/29/44/65 bytes per splat and output geometry 40/52/68/92 bytes per splat for SH0/1/2/3, plus compressed input and 9,472 shared lookup-table bytes. Same-count SH3 files differing 157.212x in compressed size produced identical decoded/output allocation, so delivery size is not a runtime-memory proxy.
items.remainingUnknown: No user photo set exists. COLMAP and Brush executables were unavailable, no training or cleanup ran, actual learned SH/DC/footprint/count distributions, real depth-bin collision frequency and perceptual importance remain unknown, and no independent float reference to r186 fixed-view GPU comparison, macOS/iPhone/Safari result or human acceptance exists. ZSTD WebAssembly allocator high-water mark, fetch/FileLoader copies, garbage-collection overlap with R40 GaussianSplat construction, browser/object/process overhead, backend GPU allocation/padding/copies, render-target cost and device failure behavior are unmeasured. GPU same-bin realization and exact raster/compositing agreement are unverified. R37-R41 fixture values and formulas are not universal image or capacity thresholds. Absolute metric scale remains gauge-dependent without a measured anchor. R34-R41 gates are coordinator Candidates with no Mother acknowledgement or target integration evidence.
items.currentBestView: Treat Gaussian splatting as a candidate observation/reconstruction tool and lossy appearance-bearing derivative, not Canonical Truth or complete Object DNA. Preserve source photos, pose solution, float checkpoint, cleanup edits, training mode and delivery metadata. Treat r186 sorting as renderer-local and R40-R41 memory arithmetic only as fixed-version CPU-visible lower bounds. Record depth/bin behavior and separate compressed size, decoded arrays, WASM/fetch/process/GPU peaks, frame time, device failure and human acceptance. Retain all R34-R41 gates; do not adopt an exact-sort replacement or device splat limit without measured benefit and cost.
